reviews.text: Brought Oscar to Mutt Ugly for his first groom. He’s a rescue dog and very nervous, so this was a big step for him. They did a great job with his cut, and he was in great form afterwards. Delighted with the experience—thank you!

I can’t recommend this place enough I’ve a very anxious and hard to deal with shih tzu after multiple attempts with other groomers I’ve finally found a place that is patient and caring with him from start to finish he’s never had a better groom the staff are amazing and so friendly
Thanks so much again from myself and Harry 🐾

Absolute five-star service from start to finish! Finding a groomer who genuinely cares and pays attention to detail can be tough, but this team is top-tier.
My dog can get quite anxious, but the staff handled him with so much patience, gentleness, and expertise. He came out looking phenomenal, smelling amazing, and—most importantly—happy and relaxed rather than stressed out. You can instantly tell how passionate they are about animals and how well-versed they are in handling different coats and temperaments.
Impeccably clean facilities, wonderful customer service, and brilliant results. I wouldn't trust anyone else with my pup now. Highly, highly recommend to any dog owner looking for the absolute best!
Great service and very friendly and knowledgeable staff

The absolute best! My reactive dog Daisy comes out smelling lovely and velvety soft. The groomers are amazing and Lisa is an absolute sweetheart.
Always look after Obi when she goes in for her groom. She is nervous around other dogs, staff always look out for her.

For the past three years, Django - our wonderful 60kg Wolfadoodle - has always received great kindness and attention by Lisa and all her staff of experienced Groomers. Once he’s had his seasonal ‘haircut’, Django never fails to be the centre of attention, attracting lots of admirers.
Lovely Lisa and the team at Mutt Ugly are great and come highly recommended

I’m unfortunately writing this review a year late, but I feel it’s important to share my experience.
I brought my tiny toy poodle, Penny (just 2 kg), in for a full grooming service. I was told it would take three hours—which already seemed excessive, but I trusted their process. When I returned to pick her up, I was informed that Penny had been so terrified she urinated twice during the grooming session. In the five years I’ve had her—across three different countries—this had never happened before, which was already a major red flag.
Things only got worse once we were home. Within an hour, Penny’s eyes became so swollen and irritated that she couldn’t even open them. The reaction was so severe she required a week of antibiotic treatment, with the frightening risk of permanent vision loss.
When I asked what products had been used, they pointed me to this shampoo: South Bark Blueberry Facial, After researching it, I found multiple reviews from other pet owners reporting similar allergic reactions in their dogs (see screenshot below). It’s shocking and unacceptable that such a product would be used without warning or consideration of its risks, especially on such a small, sensitive breed.

What should have been a routine grooming turned into a traumatic and dangerous ordeal for Penny. Pet owners trust groomers to prioritize safety and well-being—unfortunately, that trust was badly broken in this case.

I like it. They listened to what I wanted for my dog. And let me know what the condition of the fur is now. So they probably have to do. And they can cut my dog's nails!! Even though the hair is a bit short around the private part, I noticed that my dog keep going back to his butt… feel somethings not right... But everything else was good. Thank you.

We booked an 11:30 AM appointment and were surprised to learn, after arriving, that our dog have to wait before being groomed.

When asked about how long the appointmement would take and we would be able to pick up our dog, we were told "in the afternoon". When we questioned this, the groomer asked if we were in a rush. We said no but since our dog is not friendly towards stranger people/dogs, we asked if it would be better to come back later instead of leaving our dog in a stressful enviroment for hours.

The team said they would try to speed up things and get him ready sooner. After 15-20min, we passed by the front window and did not see our dog - we went inside and asked to take him home. The staff moved the other dogs around and then released ours since he was in a crate/box. I understand the need to keep dogs separated but the minimum would be to inform people beforehand their dogs would be put in a crate or tell people to bring them back later.

I can't really understand how they expect people to leave their pets in this conditions for hours - will NEVER return to this place.
